phase3_findings.description: No test checks that a one-row query-result text block still shows, in stream order, when a successful emit_text hides the final reply.
No test checks that the iteration-limit warning still shows after a successful emit_text call in the same request.
A non-empty final reply hidden after a successful emit_text is not logged, leaving no trace when a clarifying question or tool error goes unseen.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one Important checklist FAIL and four Suggestions, all below the critical threshold)

The PR is ready to merge: it hides the final reply once an `emit_text` call succeeds in a request and keeps that reply in history, and nothing found reaches the critical threshold. One internal doc sentence overstates what is hidden and should still be fixed.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings remain below the threshold → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-7: FAIL (important) — Docs: assistant text written alongside a tool call carries no marker and is excluded from the rendered answer; the hidden final reply is still saved to history [docs/internal/agent/factory.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/internal/agent/factory.md:76 says unmarked assistant text alongside a tool call is excluded from the rendered answer. components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:485-497) includes the last unmarked TEXT when any_marked_text is False (`elif not any_marked_text and i == last_unmarked_text_idx`), and the comment at 477-483 and the log at 516-524 confirm this is a deliberate fallback. A shipped path reaches it: in agent.py the tool loop breaks on MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ARGUMENT_FAILURES (1054-1083) with no marked terminal answer, and the limit-warning at 1136 is skipped because stopped_on_argument_failures is set. The stream then holds only the unmarked intermediate text, so it is rendered as the answer. The second half of the claim is true: the history write at agent.py:1107-1114 happens before the answer_prose_emitted gate at 1119. The 'excluded' half is absolute and wrong for the no-marked-text fallback.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_emit_text_final_reply.py` (lines 348-366): no test checks that a one-row query-result text block still shows, in stream order, when a successful `emit_text` hides the final reply. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py`: no test checks that the iteration-limit warning still shows after a successful `emit_text` call in the same request. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py` (lines 1115-1119): when a successful `emit_text` hides a non-empty final reply, nothing is logged, so an operator debugging a missing clarifying question has no trace. (raised by 1/5 agents)

- VC-4: FAIL (suggestion) — Assistant text written alongside a tool call is not shown to the user [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The prompt line (default.py:134) says assistant text alongside a tool call is NOT shown. agent.py:705-719 yields that text as a RichTextComponent whenever can_user_access_feature(UI_FEATURE_SHOW_TOOL_INVOCATION_MESSAGE_IN_CHAT) is true; config.py:31 grants that feature to the 'admin' group by default, so those users see it in the stream. In _format.py:486-497 the intermediate text is unmarked. Unmarked text is dropped only when any_marked_text is true. When the turn has no marked TEXT (for example an abnormal termination before the terminal-answer yield at agent.py:1119-1132, which is marked), line 496 emits the last unmarked TEXT as a public block. _format.py:477-483 and 516-524 describe this fallback. So the absolute statement is false for admin users with the feature on, and for the no-marker fallback. It holds for ordinary users and for turns that reach a marked answer.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In a `query_database` request whose result is not an error and whose blocks fit the response size budget (no truncation notice), where at least one `emit_text` call succeeds (returns a success result) and the model then ends its turn, the result's text blocks are the `emit_text` blocks and any one-row query-result text, in stream order, and none of them comes from the final reply, in both `_meta["sqllens/blocks"]` and the text content. This holds when the final reply is empty, when it repeats an `emit_text` block word for word, when it rewords one, and when its text appears in no `emit_text` block.
- [ ] In a `query_database` request whose result is not an error and where no `emit_text` call succeeds in that request — none was made, every one failed and a later data query succeeded, or the only successful one was in an earlier request of the same conversation — a non-empty final reply is shown as a text block, as today.
- [ ] A final reply that is not shown is still in the conversation history: the next request in the same conversation sends it to the model as an assistant message.
- [ ] In a request whose result is not an error and whose blocks fit the response size budget, two or more successful `emit_text` blocks are all shown, in stream order, even when their texts repeat each other; the change leaves repetition between `emit_text` blocks unchanged.
- [ ] The system prompt built by `DefaultSystemPromptBuilder` when `emit_text` is registered, and the `emit_text` tool description, state that the final reply is not shown once an `emit_text` call succeeds in a request and is shown when none succeeds, and that assistant text written alongside a tool call is not shown. Neither says that all non-`emit_text` assistant text is hidden.
- [ ] The system prompt built when `emit_text` is registered tells the model that once an `emit_text` call succeeds in a request, every sentence the user must see goes in `emit_text`, including text the other prompt rules place in its reply, such as a clarifying question, a one-row result sentence, a quoted tool error or a schema refusal.
- [ ] No code comment or docstring under `src/sqllens/`, and no page under `docs/`, states that all non-`emit_text` assistant text is hidden, or describes how the final reply is marked or whether it is shown in a way the changed code contradicts.
- [ ] Automated tests drive a real agent loop through `query_database` with a scripted model and cover: `emit_text` then an identical final reply, `emit_text` then a final reply with different text, no `emit_text` then a final reply, a failed `emit_text` then a successful data `run_sql` then a final reply, two `emit_text` blocks with repeated text, and the hidden reply's presence in the next request's history.
